name: org.getopenhealth/openhealth
title: OpenHealth
description: Public US records on nursing homes, home health and hospice; Medicare doctor and hospital data.

tools.name: find_nursing_homes
tools.description: Finds Medicare-certified nursing homes by name, by place, or both. The place can be a city with its state, such as Columbus, OH, a 5-digit ZIP code or a two-letter state. Returns up to 10 homes ordered by Medicare's overall star rating, then by name, with each home's CCN, city, beds, nurse hours, fines and owner type. When no home lists the ZIP code, it returns homes whose ZIP codes share the first three digits and says so. OpenHealth does not grade nursing homes.

name.description: Part of the nursing home's name, such as Burns Nursing Home.

place.description: A US city with its state, such as Columbus, OH, a 5-digit ZIP code, or a two-letter state code.

tools.name: get_nursing_home
tools.description: Gets one nursing home's Medicare record by its six-character CCN. The record includes Medicare's star ratings, staffing hours and turnover, the latest inspection summary and citations, fines and payment denials, owners and ownership changes, the chain, and the Special Focus Facility and abuse flags, with the source files and their dates. The ratings are Medicare's. OpenHealth adds no grade of its own.

ccn.description: The nursing home's six-character CMS Certification Number (CCN), such as 015009.

tools.name: get_nursing_home_inspection
tools.description: The tool gets one nursing home inspection by the home's six-character CCN and, optionally, the inspection date (YYYY-MM-DD). It gets the latest inspection when you omit the date. It returns each health citation with its tag, scope and severity, and the inspector's statement from Form CMS-2567 exactly as CMS publishes it. CMS removes or brackets terms that could identify a resident. OpenHealth adds nothing and summarizes nothing. The result shortens long statements, and the page shows them in full.

ccn.description: The nursing home's six-character CMS Certification Number (CCN), such as 015009.

date.description: Enter the inspection date as YYYY-MM-DD. Leave it out to get the latest inspection.

tools.name: get_nursing_home_staffing
tools.description: The tool gets a nursing home's staffing from Medicare's Payroll Based Journal by the home's six-character CCN. It returns every held quarter's summary, including nurse hours per resident per day, registered nurse hours, weekend hours, days with residents and no registered nurse hours, and contract staff share when the build carries it. It returns daily points for one quarter. Without a quarter (YYYYQn), it returns the newest quarter's daily points. A figure CMS does not publish, or a figure under the 11-person floor, is null and never zero.

ccn.description: The nursing home's six-character CMS Certification Number (CCN), such as 015009.

quarter.description: A quarter as YYYYQn, such as 2026Q2. Omit it for the newest quarter.

tools.name: compare_nursing_homes
tools.description: The tool compares two to four nursing homes by their six-character CCNs. It returns the same fields for each home side by side: Medicare's star ratings, nurse staffing hours per resident per day, staff turnover, the latest inspection summary, and fines as CMS publishes them. A missing value stays null. OpenHealth adds no grade and does not rank the homes.

ccns.description: Two to four six-character CMS Certification Numbers (CCNs).

tools.name: find_home_health_agencies
tools.description: OpenHealth finds Medicare-certified home health agencies. A 5-digit ZIP code returns the agencies Medicare lists as serving that ZIP code. A city with its state, such as Columbus, OH, or a two-letter state returns agencies with an office there. A name narrows either search. OpenHealth returns up to 10 agencies ordered by Medicare's quality of patient care star rating, then by name. Each result includes the agency's CCN and page link. OpenHealth adds no grade of its own.

name.description: Part of the agency's name, such as Ashtabula Regional.

place.description: A 5-digit ZIP code, a US city with its state, such as Columbus, OH, or a two-letter state code.

tools.name: get_home_health_agency
tools.description: OpenHealth gets one home health agency's Medicare record by its six-character CCN. The record includes Medicare's quality of patient care star rating, the patient survey stars and answers, every published quality measure with its denominator, the services the agency offers and its value-based purchasing score. Values are as CMS publishes them. A blank stays null.

ccn.description: The agency's six-character CMS Certification Number (CCN), such as 367128.

tools.name: find_hospices
tools.description: OpenHealth finds Medicare-certified hospices. A 5-digit ZIP code returns the hospices Medicare lists as serving that ZIP code. A city with its state, such as Columbus, OH, or a two-letter state returns hospices with an office there. A name narrows either search. OpenHealth returns up to 10 hospices ordered by Medicare's family caregiver survey star rating, then by name. Each result includes the hospice's CCN and page link. OpenHealth adds no grade of its own.

name.description: Part of the agency's name, such as Ashtabula Regional.

place.description: A 5-digit ZIP code, a US city with its state, such as Columbus, OH, or a two-letter state code.

tools.name: get_hospice
tools.description: OpenHealth gets one hospice's Medicare record by its six-character CCN. The record includes Medicare's family caregiver survey star rating and answers, and every published quality measure with its denominator, percentile and period, including the Hospice Care Index. Values are as CMS publishes them. A blank stays null.

ccn.description: The agency's six-character CMS Certification Number (CCN), such as 367128.

tools.name: get_facility_inspection
tools.description: The tool gets one home health or hospice inspection by type (home_health or hospice), the six-character CCN and, optionally, the survey event ID or date. It gets the latest inspection when you omit the event. It returns each finding with its tag and level and the inspector's statement from Form CMS-2567 as CMS publishes it. Each call returns five findings with an offset. Dialysis inspections are not held yet.

ccn.description: The facility's six-character CMS Certification Number (CCN).

event.description: The survey event ID or the survey date (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit it for the latest inspection.

offset.description: How many items to skip for the next page of a long list.

tools.name: get_facility_owner
tools.description: The tool gets an organization owner from Medicare's owner files by associate ID or by facility type and CCN. It returns the facilities it owns on record by setting, with role, share and start date. It returns the owner group it belongs to and the changes of ownership involving it. Each call returns 25 facilities with an offset. Individuals are counted, never named.

owner_id.description: The owner's ten-digit Medicare associate ID, as /owners pages show it.

type.description: The facility setting: nursing_home, home_health, hospice or hospital.

ccn.description: The facility's six-character CMS Certification Number (CCN).

offset.description: How many items to skip for the next page of a long list.

tools.name: find_facilities_by_owner
tools.description: The tool finds owner organizations whose published name contains every word you give. It searches Medicare's owner files for nursing homes, home health agencies, hospices and hospitals. It returns up to 10 owners with their associate ID, the number of facilities on record and the settings.

name.description: Words in the owner organization's name.

tools.name: find_care_after_hospital
tools.description: The tool lists care Medicare covers after a hospital stay near a five-digit ZIP code. It lists nursing homes and rehabilitation or long-term care hospitals with an address in ZIP codes sharing the first three digits. It lists home health agencies and hospices that list the ZIP in Medicare's files. It returns up to 5 per setting with Medicare's own figures and states each list's order. It never ranks one setting against another.

settings.description: Optional settings to list: nursing_homes, rehab_hospitals, home_health, hospice.

tools.name: get_rehab_hospital
tools.description: The tool gets an inpatient rehabilitation facility or unit, or a long-term care hospital, by its six-character CCN. It returns the address, ownership, certification, Medicare use and each quality measure under the name in CMS's own data dictionary. It returns CMS's comparison category. It counts a rehabilitation measure that no held CMS document names, but does not show it. A rehabilitation unit names the hospital it belongs to.

ccn.description: The facility's six-character CMS Certification Number (CCN).

tools.name: find_dialysis_facilities
tools.description: The tool finds dialysis facilities by city, state, ZIP code or name. It returns up to 10 facilities in the order of Medicare's star rating, then name. It returns the chain and the number of stations as CMS lists them.

place.description: A city and state, a state code or a five-digit ZIP code.

tools.name: get_dialysis_facility
tools.description: The tool gets a dialysis facility by its six-character CCN. It returns Medicare's star rating, the chain, stations and services, and every published figure in the dialysis facility file under CMS's column name. This includes death, hospital admission, readmission and transfusion rates with their confidence limits and CMS's category. A blank figure is null and never zero.

ccn.description: The facility's six-character CMS Certification Number (CCN).

tools.name: list_procedures
tools.description: Lists the procedures covered by OpenHealth, such as knee replacement, hip replacement, heart bypass and cataract surgery. Each procedure has an id and an OpenHealth page. The list shows which procedures have hospital results and which do not. Use the list to find the procedure id for a doctor search. This tool takes no input. Procedure counts and hospital results come from Medicare data only, so they are incomplete.

tools.name: find_doctors_for_procedure
tools.description: This tool finds doctors with public records for a procedure near a US city or ZIP code, such as a knee replacement surgeon near me. It returns up to 5 doctors, ordered by nearest office first. Each doctor includes distance, Medicare yearly procedure count, and CMS-listed affiliated hospitals. For procedures with hospital results, each hospital is better than, no different from, or worse than the national rate. OpenHealth does not grade or rank doctors. The better_hospital_only filter keeps doctors with a better hospital. The radius is 10, 25 or 50 miles. These Medicare records are incomplete.

procedure.description: The procedure, as an id such as knee-replacement or in plain words such as knee replacement.

place.description: A US city with its state, such as Columbus, OH, or a 5-digit ZIP code.

radius_miles.description: The search radius in miles: 10, 25 or 50. The default is 25.

better_hospital_only.description: When true, the tool lists only doctors affiliated with at least one hospital whose result is better than the national rate. The default is false.

tools.name: search_providers
tools.description: Searches OpenHealth's public records for a doctor or hospital by name. Returns up to 10 matches with the doctor's NPI or the hospital's CCN, the city, the state and the OpenHealth page. A hospital search needs a two-letter state. A doctor search can be narrowed by state. When no doctor has the exact name, it returns doctors with similar names and marks them. Doctor and hospital records on OpenHealth come from Medicare data only and are incomplete.

name.description: The doctor's or hospital's name, such as Matthew Bernhard or Riverside Methodist.

state.description: A two-letter US state code, such as OH.

kind.description: doctor or hospital. The default is doctor.

tools.name: get_doctor
tools.description: This tool gets one doctor's public record by 10-digit NPI. The record lists offices, specialties, and affiliated hospitals. It lists hospital results for each procedure that has them. It lists federal exclusion-list checks, state medical board actions matched by license number in states OpenHealth covers, and published procedure counts and outcome measures with their sources. A hospital result describes a hospital, not the doctor. OpenHealth gives doctors no grade or score. The counts and measures are Medicare records only, so they are incomplete.

tools.name: check_doctor_insurance
tools.description: Checks which insurance plan directories list a doctor, by NPI or by name with an optional state, and optionally for one insurer such as Aetna, Cigna or Medicare. Returns each listing with its plans, its update date and whether the directory lists the doctor as accepting new patients, plus Medicare and Medicaid billing. No listing means unknown, not out of network. A listing does not confirm coverage. Only the plan can confirm it.

doctor_name.description: The doctor's full name, such as Matthew Bernhard. Use it when you have no NPI.

state.description: A two-letter US state code, such as OH.

insurer.description: One insurer to check, using one of the listed ids, such as aetna or medicare.

tools.name: get_hospital
tools.description: Gets one hospital's public record by CCN, or by name with a two-letter state. The record includes the address, CMS overall star rating, hospital type, owners from CMS ownership records, private equity flag, last ownership change, published outcome measures, and whether OpenHealth holds a current price file for the hospital. The outcome measures come from Medicare data only. They leave out patients with other insurance, so they are incomplete.

ccn.description: The hospital's six-character CMS Certification Number (CCN), such as 360006.

name.description: The hospital's name, such as Riverside Methodist Hospital. Use it with state when you have no CCN.

state.description: A two-letter US state code, such as OH. A hospital name needs this code.

tools.name: get_hospital_prices
tools.description: Gets a hospital's published price for a service, such as a head CT, chest X-ray, knee MRI, colonoscopy or knee replacement, or for a CPT code. Takes the hospital's CCN, or its name with a two-letter state, and an optional insurer. Returns the cash price and insurer rates as published in the hospital's own price file, with the file and its read date. A price is not a personal quote, is not checked against a plan network and is not the total cost of care. OpenHealth does not show a file read more than 30 days ago.

ccn.description: The hospital's six-character CMS Certification Number (CCN), such as 360006.

hospital.description: The hospital's name, such as Riverside Methodist Hospital. Use it with state when you have no CCN.

state.description: A two-letter US state code, such as OH. A hospital name needs this code.

service.description: The service or procedure, as one of the listed ids, such as head-ct-without-contrast or knee-replacement.

cpt_code.description: A five-character CPT or HCPCS code, such as 70450. Use it when no service id fits.

insurer.description: One insurer to check, using one of the listed ids, such as aetna or medicare.

tools.name: get_doctor_payments
tools.description: Gets the general payments that drug and device companies reported to CMS Open Payments for one doctor, by 10-digit NPI. Returns totals by program year and by company, with the payment types, and the doctor's Medicare Part D prescriptions of drugs named in those payments where the files have them. A payment is not a sign of wrongdoing. The overlap with prescriptions does not show that a payment changed a prescription.

tools.name: search_drugs
tools.description: Searches drugs by brand or generic name, such as metformin or Eliquis. Returns up to 10 matches with each drug's RxCUI, its name and form, whether it is a brand or a generic, and how many marketplace plan drug lists name it. Use the RxCUI with get_drug.

name.description: The drug's brand or generic name, such as metformin or Eliquis.

tools.name: get_drug
tools.description: Gets the public figures for one drug by RxCUI: NADAC, which is what pharmacies pay to buy the drug and not a retail price, Medicare Part D spending, state Medicaid spending by year, and how many marketplace plan drug lists name the drug, with their tiers and limits. None of these figures is what a person pays at the pharmacy. A plan list that does not name the drug is unknown, not a sign that the plan does not cover it.

rxcui.description: The drug's RxNorm concept ID (RxCUI), such as 861004. search_drugs returns it.

tools.name: find_health_plans
tools.description: Finds marketplace health plans in a state for a plan year, optionally narrowed by plan name, insurer or plan ID. Returns up to 20 plans ordered by deductible, low to high, then by name, as the site lists them, with each plan's ID, metal level, insurer, deductible and out-of-pocket maximum as the CMS file states them, and its drug list size. Premiums are not in the public file. The amounts are not a quote for you.

state.description: A two-letter US state code, such as OH.

query.description: Words from the plan name or the insurer name, or a plan ID.

year.description: The plan year, such as 2027. The default is the latest year OpenHealth reads.

tools.name: get_health_plan
tools.description: Gets one marketplace health plan by its 14-character plan ID and plan year. Returns the metal level, plan type, insurer, deductibles and out-of-pocket maximums as the CMS file states them, the drug list counts by tier with prior approval, step therapy and quantity limit counts, the size of the insurer's directory for the plan, and links to the plan documents. The amounts are not a quote for you.

plan_id.description: The 14-character plan ID from the plan documents, such as 31274WV0560001.

year.description: The plan year, such as 2027. The default is the latest year OpenHealth reads.

tools.name: get_data_sources
tools.description: Lists the public data sources behind OpenHealth's nursing home, home health, hospice, doctor and hospital records, such as CMS files and state reports, with each source's link and review date, and the current data release.
